original_test_intent: Measure random write bandwidth and IOPS on the approved Windows storage target using CrystalDiskMark and compare the displayed result with the project specification.
original_method: A qualified operator records platform/device/tool identity, selects an approved disposable target or safe test file and random-write profile, runs once with approved size/count, exports the full result table, records health/events and leaves cleanup to owner.
manual_activity: Qualified operator controls Windows GUI, verifies disposable target/test-file scope, runs only approved random-write profile and captures evidence.
required_inputs: Approved Windows SUT and CrystalDiskMark version/checksum
Exact storage model/serial/firmware/drive letter and disposable target or safe test-file scope
Random-write profile, size/count, cache/power policy and duration
Versioned write MB/s/IOPS thresholds with tolerance
Data-loss authorization, health/thermal abort and cleanup policy
safety_requirements: Verify drive identity and write scope before Start
Do not use OS/production/in-use target or default suite without approval
Stop on wrong target/profile, unexpected scope, device/thermal error or instability
No automatic retry, format, deletion or restoration
agent_execution_scope: Review operator-supplied version, target, profile, screenshot/export and health evidence
Compare recorded metrics with thresholds without claiming GUI control
Do not operate GUI, infer clicks, fabricate results or issue verdict
engineer_actions: Provide target, write profile, threshold and data-loss authorization
Ensure qualified operator captures complete evidence

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Correctly rejects SSH execution but lacks destructive target, profile reproducibility and health/cleanup controls.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: MANUAL ONLY: operator runs exact random-write CrystalDiskMark item on approved target and saves unmodified table.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Random write, bandwidth/IOPS, Windows CrystalDiskMark and20/30 planning fields are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use signed operator checklist binding drive serial, GUI build, random-write item, size/count and thresholds to screenshot/export evidence.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds safe write scope, reproducibility, identity, health and controlled cleanup.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Other GUI rows or CLI benchmarks are not substitutes without approved equivalence.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Random writes are destructive and results depend on cache, free space, conditioning, thermal state and GUI settings.

project_override_considerations: Project-specific profile and specification are readiness inputs; the GUI default suite and other tools cannot be silently substituted.
expected_evidence: Operator/date plus Windows and CrystalDiskMark identities
Exact target model/serial/firmware/drive letter and approved write scope
Random-write profile, size/count and unmodified screenshot/export
Displayed write MB/s and IOPS mapped to thresholds
GUI exit, no unintended process and owner-directed cleanup

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Title, Windows GUI procedure and spec comparison align. Missing target/profile/threshold values are readiness inputs; broad read/write wording is constrained by the named random-write item.

blocked_analysis.analysis: A Windows operator can perform the GUI write test when the safe target and inputs are supplied; this is MANUAL ONLY rather than inherently blocked.

review_improvement: Adds destructive target authorization, reproducible GUI profile and verifiable evidence without pretending remote automation.
independent_technical_reasoning: Random write touches dispersed logical blocks or a generated test file and can alter data or stress flash translation and garbage collection. The result depends on queue/thread settings, size and device state, all selected in the GUI. Only operator-captured profile plus exact drive identity can establish what ran safely.
